balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by reporting segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Boston Scientific runs two reporting segments: Cardiovascular (interventional/structural heart, electrophysiology, peripheral and rhythm management) and MedSurg (endoscopy, urology and neuromodulation).

For Boston Scientific Corporation: Cardiovascular is now roughly two-thirds of revenue and has been growing faster than MedSurg, driven by Watchman and the interventional-cardiology franchise — the mix shift raises the company's growth rate but concentrates it in one segment.

What to watch:

  • Whether MedSurg growth is reaccelerating or still lagging Cardiovascular
  • Segment mix shift versus the consolidated growth rate on the main Revenue chart

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Segment operating income
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Operating income reported by each segment, before corporate costs and unallocated items are allocated back to the consolidated income statement.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: Cardiovascular's segment margin is structurally higher than MedSurg's, so the revenue mix shift toward Cardiovascular also lifts consolidated operating margin.

What to watch:

  • Segment margin trend, not just segment revenue growth
  • Gap between the sum of segment operating income and consolidated operating income (corporate/unallocated costs)

usIntl.title: US vs international revenue
usIntl.content:
Revenue split between the US and international markets.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the US is still the larger and faster-growing market on new-product launches (Watchman, Farapulse); international growth depends more on reimbursement and tender timing.

What to watch:

  • International growth catching up to, or lagging, the US
  • FX translation effects on the international line in a strong-dollar period

intlMix.title: International revenue by region
intlMix.content:
International revenue broken into EMEA, Asia-Pacific, Emerging Markets and Latin America/Canada (LACA).

For Boston Scientific Corporation: Emerging Markets and Asia-Pacific have grown fastest of the four, while LACA remains the smallest region by a wide margin.

What to watch:

  • Any single region decelerating sharply (tender losses, FX, local competition)
  • Emerging Markets' growing share of the international total

cardioMix.title: Cardiovascular revenue by product category
cardioMix.content:
Cardiovascular segment revenue by product category: ICVT (Interventional Cardiology & Vascular Therapies), IOE, Electrophysiology, CRM (Cardiac Rhythm Management) and Watchman.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: Watchman (left atrial appendage closure) and Electrophysiology (Farapulse pulsed-field ablation) are the two fastest-growing categories and the main reason Cardiovascular is outgrowing MedSurg; CRM is the slow-growth legacy pacemaker/defibrillator business.

What to watch:

  • Watchman and Electrophysiology growth rates versus the segment average
  • CRM share shrinking as a percentage of the segment

medSurgMix.title: MedSurg revenue by product category
medSurgMix.content:
MedSurg segment revenue by product category: Endoscopy, Urology and Neuromodulation.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: Endoscopy is the largest of the three and sets the segment's growth rate; Neuromodulation is the smallest and has historically grown more slowly than the other two.

What to watch:

  • Whether any one category is dragging down overall MedSurg growth
  • Endoscopy's share given its weight in the segment total

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Boston Scientific Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
